summary: The workflow is coherent on the points the prior critique targeted: leadership/peer direction is symmetric, the recursion guard is stated in both the skill and the packet instruction, absence is explicitly never a pass, and human authority is preserved at the author-gate. The declined items (third local pass, new engine hash command) are defensible on the stated grounds. The remaining defects are in the mechanics the workflow now leans on. Hash-based staleness detection is the load-bearing mechanism for reuse, resume and cross-host comparison, but no computation procedure is pinned, so two hosts will not reproduce a digest. The architect skill's allowed-tools frontmatter does not cover the isolated-peer procedure it mandates, which pressures agents toward weakening the invocation. Round accounting charges a lead-side packet defect against the design-review budget. ADR immutability is contradicted by the acceptance procedure that edits the file after it lands in adr/. And the --from-spec import path skips stage 2 entirely, which is where the binding "every risk becomes a decision or [accepted-risk]" rule lives.

findings.evidence: coverage.md: "Use repo-relative paths plus SHA-256 of current UTF-8 file content, omitting only whole `<!-- stage: N -->` marker lines from architecture documents"; "Hash once before sending and recheck after the peer returns"; "On resume, read the repo's own record and response, compare input hashes and scope". A `harness hash` command was explicitly declined.
findings.requirement: Either host may lead or resume; coverage reuse and material-change detection depend on comparing hashes across hosts and sessions.
findings.consequence: The normalization is described but not specified: whether the omitted line's newline is also removed, whether the rule applies to any file containing a marker or only docs/architecture.md, whether trailing-newline/CRLF are normalized, and by what command. A Claude-led session and a Codex-led resume will produce different digests for a byte-identical file. Divergence presents as a material change, which either burns the two-round budget on phantom deltas or trains agents to hand-wave "recomputed, unchanged" — the same failure the fingerprints were introduced to close. Hand-asserted digests are also unverifiable by the human reading the record.
findings.suggestion: Pin one literal command in coverage.md that both hosts must use and record it in the record: `grep -v '^<!-- stage: [0-9][0-9]* -->$' docs/architecture.md | shasum -a 256` for the working document only, and plain `shasum -a 256 <file>` for every other input. State that the filter applies to exactly that one path, so no per-file judgement is needed. This stays authored-record-only and needs no engine change.
findings.uncertainty: If the plugin already ships a documented hashing helper referenced outside the supplied files, this is redundant. Nothing in the supplied text names one, and the decision record says a hash command was declined.

findings.evidence: skills/architect/SKILL.md frontmatter: `allowed-tools: Bash(*/bin/harness *) Bash(codex exec *) Bash(claude -p *)`, against peer-cli.md: "Create a unique temporary directory outside the project, put the review packet there", "Write stdout, stderr and final output to distinct, newly created paths", "Follow local command wrappers such as RTK", "Do not weaken permissions to make a review run"; plus coverage.md's SHA-256 requirement and architect stage 5's `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/harness" author-gate`.
findings.requirement: Claude Code must be able to run Codex as peer from the Claude host without degrading the isolation the skill specifies.
findings.consequence: The mandated procedure needs commands the list does not admit: creating the external temp dir, writing packet.md and the schema copy there, computing hashes, reading stderr.log/critique.json, and the RTK-wrapped form (`rtk proxy codex exec ...`) which does not match `codex exec *`. Entries are space-separated rather than comma-separated, so the list may parse as a single malformed entry. The quoted harness invocations in the body (`"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/harness" author-gate --report ...`) do not match `*/bin/harness *` because of the closing quote before the space. Under a restrictive whitelist the review stalls on denials mid-run, and the likely agent workaround is to drop isolation flags to fit an allowed pattern — precisely the prohibited weakening.
findings.suggestion: Either remove `allowed-tools` from architect/SKILL.md and let the host permission mode govern, or fix it to match reality: comma-separate entries, cover the quoted harness form, and add the file-write/read and hashing commands the peer procedure requires. Note in peer-cli.md that if the required commands are not permitted, the correct outcome is to record the peer unavailable with that reason — never a reduced-isolation invocation.
findings.uncertainty: Skill-frontmatter allowed-tools semantics (hard whitelist vs advisory) and exact prefix-matching behavior are not verifiable from the supplied text; Codex ignores this field, so only the Claude-lead direction is affected.

findings.evidence: coverage.md: "A round is one schema-valid peer response, including `insufficient-context`. Missing CLI detection and failed/invalid invocations are attempts, not completed rounds." SKILL.md step 5: "Missing inputs can use the one focused follow-up"; step 6: "After two rounds, record later material changes as `superseded`."
findings.requirement: Bounded effort must still deliver at least one real critique of the design when the peer is available.
findings.consequence: An `insufficient-context` result usually signals a lead-side packet defect (wrong excerpts, paths without content, missing hashes), not a design iteration. Charging it as round 1 and the remediation resend as round 2 exhausts the budget with zero assessments of the design, after which every later material change is recorded `superseded` and the collaboration requirement is formally satisfied while never having happened. This is also asymmetric with invalid output, which correctly costs nothing though it likewise delivers no critique.
findings.suggestion: Count toward the two-round limit only responses whose assessment is `ready` or `concerns`. Allow exactly one packet-remediation resend after `insufficient-context`, recorded as an attempt with the specific inputs that were missing, and cap it so a peer that keeps reporting insufficient-context terminates as a recorded limitation rather than looping.
findings.uncertainty: This may be a deliberate anti-looping choice. If kept as-is, the docs should at least say what the lead does when the budget is spent and the design has never been assessed — currently step 6 and coverage.md both route to `superseded` without distinguishing that case.

findings.evidence: adr-authoring/SKILL.md: "Accepted files are `adr/NNN-kebab-title.md`, numbered sequentially and immutable" alongside "move the reviewed draft into `adr/`, set its accepted status and compile". coverage.md: "Accepted ADRs are immutable: put the link in their proposed successor, never patch the accepted file" and "Recompute hashes after correcting relative links".
findings.requirement: Proposed ADRs must be reviewed and linked before acceptance without violating the immutability rule that protects accepted records.
findings.consequence: The acceptance procedure necessarily edits a file already sitting at `adr/NNN-...md`: the status transition, and the relative link to `docs/design-reviews/` which resolves differently from `adr/` than from `docs/design-reviews/drafts/`. The text never says when immutability attaches. A cautious agent refuses to edit and leaves `status: proposed` in `adr/` — which adr-authoring itself warns can retire the accepted predecessor via `supersedes` on the next compile. A permissive agent cites the same acceptance-in-progress framing to edit genuinely accepted ADRs later.
findings.suggestion: State that immutability attaches after the first successful `compile` of the file in `adr/`, and define the acceptance transaction as exactly two permitted post-move edits — status transition and relative link correction — both required before that compile. Record the post-move digest as `current hash` in the Changes-since-review row so the move is auditable rather than silent.
findings.uncertainty: The compiler may already enforce immutability mechanically; bin/harness behavior is not supplied. If it does, the docs still disagree with it and should be aligned.

findings.evidence: architect/SKILL.md: `--from-spec` "writes `docs/architecture.md` at `<!-- stage: 3 -->`" and "continue at stage 3 below". The binding rule lives only in stage-redteam.md: "every risk raised must resolve into either a decision or an explicit `[accepted-risk]` block ... silently dropped risks are a defect", together with the md-file-bug silent-failure hunt. stage-converge.md checks review coverage for imports but restates no risk-disposition rule. Separately, coverage.md says to "record `import-derived`" while the record structure's `Coverage:` line enumerates only `current | incomplete | superseded | none`.
findings.requirement: Imported specs still need this repo's own review, and peer findings must survive synthesis rather than being summarized away.
findings.consequence: An imported platform spec — the case with the most unexamined inherited assumptions — reaches convergence without the local premortem and without any rule forcing peer-raised risks into decisions or `[accepted-risk]` blocks. design-review step 4 mentions accepted-risk blocks, but the binding, exit-criteria-backed version is unreachable on this path, and author-gate checks decision rows and open questions, not risk dispositions. The `import-derived` marker has no field in the record structure, so the fresh-review-for-imports fix degrades to prose an agent may not write down.
findings.suggestion: Require the stage-2 local red-team pass and its binding risk-resolution rule on the `--from-spec` path before stage-3 convergence (either by seeding at stage 2, or by restating the binding rule in stage-converge.md for imports). Add a `Provenance: native | import-derived | resumed` line to the coverage record structure so the import case is recordable.
findings.uncertainty: agents/red-team.md, the premortem checklist and the author-gate implementation are not supplied; the gate may already require risk dispositions, which would reduce this to the missing record field.

alternative: A simpler option that meets the same requirement with less machinery: replace per-file SHA-256 fingerprints with a byte-for-byte snapshot of the packet and its input files stored beside the record under `docs/design-reviews/<topic>-<revision>/`. Staleness then becomes `diff -r` against the working tree instead of a hand-computed digest with a prose normalization rule, which removes F1 entirely (no marker-line filter, no cross-host reproducibility question, no before/after recompute step) and makes every coverage claim independently checkable by the human reading the record. It costs repository bytes — bounded, since the packet is already required to be focused excerpts rather than whole repositories — and it needs one explicit instruction to exclude builder transcripts and `.harness/memory/session/`, which the skill already states. Round budget, the peer response schema, the ADR acceptance flow and the human author-gate stay exactly as designed. Worth weighing against F1's fix (pinning one hash command), which is cheaper to adopt but keeps the record unverifiable by inspection.
missing_context: response.schema.json — its contents were not supplied, so I could not verify that the field set required by SKILL.md step 3 and the packet instruction (severity, evidence, requirement, consequence, fix, uncertainty) matches the assessment enum in coverage.md, or that the Claude peer's structured_output and the Codex peer's --output-schema validate against the same document.
agents/red-team.md and the premortem skill's silent-failure checklist, referenced by stage-redteam.md — needed to judge F5's severity and whether risk dispositions are enforced anywhere mechanical.
bin/harness behavior for author-gate and compile: whether the gate checks [accepted-risk] blocks and review coverage, and whether the compiler enforces adr/ immutability (bears on F4 and F5).

Installed CLI help for the flags used in peer-cli.md — `claude --tools`, `--json-schema`, `--no-session-persistence`, `--disable-slash-commands`, and the `codex exec --disable ...` set. The doc correctly says to read help first, but the Codex section has an explicit "record unavailable with the reason" fallback that the Claude section lacks; I could not verify the flags to judge whether that asymmetry matters.
An example completed record under docs/design-reviews/ — would show whether the record structure is workable in practice, particularly the Inputs before/after hash row and the import/resume cases.
